chapter: Later tours, illness and the union job
title: Drinking slivovitch in Yugoslavia with Joe Turner
summary: On a State Department trip with Turner, Armstrong warned him off slivovitch, which they dismissed until they drank it.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: Well what was that time you went to Yugoslavia? What what is that happened there?
As far as, as close as I can come to it SLIVOVTCH.
Now what were you doing in Yugoslavia? Was that a festival?
We went over for the State Department. Just Joe Turner and I. We went from England over there to play.
You mean Joe Turner the blues singer?
Yes. We went over there to play this festival, three-day festival. First thing we, I'd seen Louis.
Yes. We met Louis, I met Louis, where was it, somewhere I saw Louis over there and he says, Buck, don't mess with that Slivovitch. (LAUGHTER). So that's the first thing I wanted to do.

It's made out of prunes and it's strong, you know. And so me and Joe Turner we got in Yugoslavia, got comfortably seated in a bar and we proce ded to take a drink of Slivovitch. And it just went down like apple juice. It went down, so we said, Slivovitch isn't, it isn't nothing.

So we met a lot of Yugoslavian musicians and I remember they were mixing it up with, they were mixing it up with rum. Slivovitch and rum together. I remember I was talking to one of them; he was a trumpet player and the guy just fell out, flat fell right on his face at the bar from mixing this stuff.
